_meta.description: The SIMPLE structure profile, and the default one (openspec/changes/simple-structure-profile). `menu-layout.json` is the FULL profile and is untouched: an administrator brings it back with the setting `menu_structure`. Both profiles are built from the same manifest and the same fragments, so nothing is deleted and every page stays routable; this file only decides what the navigation offers first. THE STANDARD KEYS (`removals`, `settingsSection`) go to the library's buildManifest exactly as the full file's do. `relocations` is ABSENT on purpose, and must stay absent rather than become `{}`: the simple menu is flat, and the library's relocation step ends by dropping every entry that has no route, no href, no action and no children, which is what a caption is. THE PROFILE KEYS `menu` and `pages` are read by src/utils/structureProfile.js. `menu` is merged BEFORE the manifest's own menu; buildManifest merges entries by id and the FIRST definition of a key wins, so an entry here that carries only `id` and `order` keeps its label, icon and route from the manifest, and an entry the manifest does not know (the captions, Contact moments, Appointments, Organisations, Modules and more) is added as written. `pages` holds page overlays. THE PIPELINQ KEYS `modules`, `modulesCaption` and `home` are read by src/utils/menuModules.js.
_meta.removalsNote: The first six are the full profile's own removals, repeated because buildManifest takes ONE list; the spec fails when the two drift. The rest leave the simple menu and stay one step away: `Contacts`, `Tasks` and `OperationalDashboard` have a card on the Modules page, `SlaAttainment` a card on Reports, and `Bookings` is replaced by `AppointmentsMenu`, which opens the same page from the top level. `PointOfSale` and `SettingsIntegrationsCaption` are empty shells in the manifest (a label and no route). The full profile loses the second to the relocation step's clean-up and fills the first with children; this profile has no relocation step, so both are removed by name. The ids of a module that is switched off are added to this list at boot, by applyMenuModules.
_meta.settingsNote: The first three are the full profile's. `Services` and `Resources` join them: what can be booked and with whom is set-up, the bookings themselves are daily work.
_meta.viewsNote: `ContactMomentsMenu` opens the tickets list narrowed to ticketType `interaction`, and `OrganisationsMenu` the clients list narrowed to type `organization`. Both values are enum members of the seeded schema (register.d/99-unify-ticket-supertype.json, pipelinq_register.json), so they are the same on every instance. A filtered list is a view, not a page. Known gap: CnAppNav decides `active` by route name and ignores `query`, so each pair lights up together.
_meta.modulesNote: A module is a set of menu entries that a municipality does not need and a business does. Every module is OFF in the simple menu until an administrator names it in the setting `menu_modules` (a comma separated list of the keys below). `ids` are the manifest entries that leave the menu while the module is off. `menu` is what joins the profile menu when it is on, under the one caption `modulesCaption` declares. Off or on, every entry has a card on the Modules page (src/manifest.d/98-modules.json), which the footer entry `ModulesMenu` opens. The full profile ignores modules: it shows everything, as before.
_meta.homeNote: The app opens on `/`, and `/` is the Sales overview. In the simple profile the contact centre dashboard is the start page: `/` redirects to `home.page`, and the page that owned `/` moves to `home.rootMovesTo` so it keeps an address of its own. The full profile has no `home` and keeps `/` as it was.
